Apple___Apple_scab.about: Fungal disease causing olive-green to dark scabby spots on leaves and fruit.
treatment: Remove and destroy fallen and infected leaves.
Apply a fungicide recommended locally, starting at early leaf stage.
prevention: Rake up leaf litter in autumn.
Plant scab-resistant varieties and prune for airflow.

Apple___Black_rot.about: Fungal disease causing brown leaf spots, fruit rot and cankers on branches.
treatment: Prune out dead wood and cankers and destroy them.
Remove mummified fruit and apply a recommended fungicide during the growing season.
prevention: Keep trees pruned and well spaced for airflow.
Clean up fallen fruit and leaves each season.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.about: Fungal disease with bright yellow-orange spots on leaves; it needs both apple and juniper or cedar to complete its life cycle.
treatment: Remove infected leaves where practical.
Apply a recommended fungicide from the pink bud stage, as advised locally.
prevention: Remove nearby juniper or cedar galls if possible.
Choose rust-resistant apple varieties.

Apple___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Prune for airflow and clear fallen leaves.
Water at the base and check leaves regularly.

Blueberry___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep soil acidic (pH about 4.5 to 5.5) and mulched.
Water at the base and avoid wetting leaves late in the day.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.about: Fungal disease producing white powdery patches on leaves; leaves may curl or distort.
treatment: Remove heavily infected shoots and leaves.
Apply sulfur or another fungicide recommended locally, following the label.
prevention: Prune to open up the canopy and improve airflow.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer, which encourages soft growth.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Prune for airflow and clear fallen leaves.
Water at the base and watch for early signs of disease.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.about: Fungal disease causing long, narrow, rectangular tan to gray spots between leaf veins.
treatment: Apply a foliar fungicide if the disease is spreading before tasseling, as advised locally.
Manage infected crop residue after harvest.
prevention: Rotate with non-corn crops.
Plant resistant hybrids and avoid dense planting.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.about: Fungal disease with small reddish-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces.
treatment: Apply a foliar fungicide if infection is severe early in the season.
Monitor regularly; mild late infections often need no treatment.
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids.
Scout fields regularly during cool, humid weather.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.about: Fungal disease causing long, cigar-shaped gray-green to tan lesions on leaves.
treatment: Apply a foliar fungicide if lesions reach the upper leaves around tasseling.
Manage infected crop residue after harvest.
prevention: Use resistant hybrids.
Rotate crops and avoid growing corn after corn.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Rotate crops and use certified seed.
Scout fields regularly for early signs of disease.

Grape___Black_rot.about: Fungal disease causing brown circular leaf spots and shriveled black mummified berries.
treatment: Remove mummified berries and infected leaves.
Apply a recommended fungicide from early shoot growth through bloom.
prevention: Prune and train vines for sun and airflow.
Clean up fallen fruit and debris after harvest.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).about: Wood-rotting fungal complex causing tiger-stripe leaf patterns, spotted berries and vine decline.
treatment: No cure exists. Prune out infected wood in dry weather and destroy it.
Severely affected vines may need to be removed.
prevention: Protect pruning wounds and avoid pruning in wet weather.
Use clean tools and healthy planting material.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.about: Fungal disease causing dark brown irregular spots on older leaves, leading to early leaf drop.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and debris.
Apply a recommended fungicide if the disease spreads.
prevention: Improve airflow through pruning and spacing.
Avoid overhead watering and clear fallen leaves.

Grape___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Prune and train vines for airflow.
Clean up fallen fruit and leaves each season.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).about: Bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid; causes blotchy yellow leaves and small, bitter, misshapen fruit.
treatment: No cure exists. Remove and destroy infected trees to protect others.
Control psyllids with locally recommended methods.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery trees.
Monitor for psyllids and report suspected cases to local agriculture authorities.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.about: Bacterial disease causing small angular leaf spots, shot-hole damage and spotted fruit.
treatment: Apply copper-based or other products recommended locally, at the right growth stage.
Prune out badly affected twigs.
prevention: Plant tolerant varieties.
Avoid overhead irrigation and excess nitrogen fertilizer.

Peach___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Prune for an open canopy and clear fallen leaves.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.about: Bacterial disease causing small water-soaked spots that turn brown on leaves and fruit.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants and debris.
Copper-based sprays may slow spread but cannot cure infected plants.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Rotate crops and avoid working among wet plants.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Use certified seed and rotate crops.
Water at the base and check plants regularly.

Potato___Early_blight.about: Fungal disease causing dark spots with concentric rings (target-like) on older leaves.
treatment: Remove heavily infected lower leaves.
Apply a protectant fungicide recommended locally.
prevention: Rotate crops and clear plant debris after harvest.
Keep plants well fed and watered to reduce stress.

Potato___Late_blight.about: Fast-spreading disease causing dark, water-soaked patches on leaves and stems, often with white mold underneath in humid weather.
treatment: Act quickly: remove and destroy infected plants.
Apply a recommended fungicide to protect healthy plants nearby.
prevention: Use certified seed potatoes and destroy volunteer plants and cull piles.
Avoid overhead watering and plant in well-drained soil.

Potato___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Use certified seed potatoes and rotate crops.
Hill soil over tubers and check leaves regularly.

Raspberry___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Prune old canes and thin new ones for airflow.
Water at the base and remove fallen debris.

Soybean___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Rotate crops and use certified, disease-tolerant seed.
Scout fields regularly and keep weeds under control.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.about: Fungal disease producing a white powdery coating on leaves, which weakens plants and reduces yield.
treatment: Remove badly infected leaves.
Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or another recommended fungicide, following the label.
prevention: Space plants for airflow and sunlight.
Plant resistant varieties and avoid excess nitrogen.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.about: Fungal disease causing purple to dark red spots that merge, making leaves look scorched.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Apply a recommended fungicide if the disease is severe.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties and avoid overcrowding.
Water at the base and clear old leaves after harvest.

Strawberry___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Space plants and remove old or dead leaves.
Water at the base and keep beds free of debris.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.about: Bacterial disease causing small dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves and rough spots on fruit.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants and debris.
Copper-based sprays may slow spread but cannot cure infected plants.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Rotate crops and avoid handling plants when wet.

Tomato___Early_blight.about: Fungal disease causing dark spots with concentric rings, starting on lower leaves.
treatment: Remove infected lower leaves.
Apply a protectant fungicide recommended locally.
prevention: Mulch and stake plants to keep leaves off the soil.
Rotate crops and water at the base.

Tomato___Late_blight.about: Fast-spreading disease causing large, dark, water-soaked patches on leaves, stems and fruit.
treatment: Act quickly: remove and destroy infected plants.
Apply a recommended fungicide to protect healthy plants nearby.
prevention: Avoid overhead watering; water at the base in the morning.
Space plants well and destroy infected debris at the end of the season.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.about: Fungal disease causing pale yellow spots on top of leaves with olive-gray mold underneath, common in humid conditions.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve ventilation.
Apply a recommended fungicide if it keeps spreading.
prevention: Lower humidity and avoid wetting leaves, especially in greenhouses.
Choose resistant varieties and space plants well.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.about: Fungal disease causing many small round spots with gray centers and dark edges on lower leaves.
treatment: Remove infected leaves.
Apply a recommended protectant fungicide.
prevention: Mulch, stake and water at the base.
Rotate crops and clear plant debris after harvest.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.about: Tiny pests (not a disease) that suck sap, causing yellow speckling, fine webbing and leaf drop, mostly in hot, dry weather.
treatment: Spray plants with a strong stream of water; use insecticidal soap or horticultural oil as directed.
Remove heavily infested leaves.
prevention: Keep plants well watered; dust and drought stress favor mites.
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural predators.

Tomato___Target_Spot.about: Fungal disease causing brown spots with concentric rings on leaves, stems and fruit.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and debris.
Apply a recommended fungicide if it spreads.
prevention: Improve airflow by staking and spacing plants.
Rotate crops and avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.about: Virus spread by whiteflies; causes upward-curled, yellow, stunted leaves and poor fruit set.
treatment: No cure exists. Remove and destroy infected plants.
Control whiteflies with netting, reflective mulch or locally recommended methods.
prevention: Use virus-resistant varieties and healthy transplants.
Monitor for whiteflies and control weeds nearby.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.about: Virus causing mottled light and dark green leaves, distortion and reduced yield; it spreads by touch and tools.
treatment: No cure exists. Remove and destroy infected plants.
Wash hands and disinfect tools after handling them.
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed and resistant varieties.
Wash hands after using tobacco before handling plants.

Tomato___healthy.about: No disease detected. The leaf looks healthy.
treatment: No treatment needed.
prevention: Water at the base and stake plants for airflow.
Rotate crops and check leaves regularly.
